question: A woman who underwent FGM as a child is admitted in active labor. What is she at higher risk for during delivery?

options.A: Rapid, painless delivery due to relaxed pelvic muscles
options.B: Obstructed labor and severe tearing from scar tissue
options.C: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.D: Instant healing of the perineal area after birth

explanation: Scar tissue from FGM lacks elasticity, often blocking the birth canal and causing severe tearing during childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h3)

question: What makes a reflex a 'monosynaptic' reflex?

options.A: It requires conscious thought from the cerebral cortex.
options.B: It involves multiple interneurons inside the brainstem.
options.C: It controls internal smooth muscle organs exclusively.
options.D: It has only one synapse between the sensory and motor neuron.

explanation: Mono means one! A monosynaptic reflex skips the interneuron middleman entirely, going straight from sensory to motor for lightning speed.

question: Which parts of the body are involved in a lower respiratory tract infection?

options.A: Sinuses, tonsils, and Eustachian tubes
options.B: Nose, pharynx, and larynx
options.C: Oral cavity and epiglottis
options.D: Trachea, bronchi, and alveoli

explanation: Think of the larynx as the dividing line! Anything below it—like the windpipe (trachea), breathing tubes (bronchi), and air sacs (alveoli)—makes up the lower respiratory tract.

question: What is the main goal of psychiatric-mental health nursing?

options.A: Confining dangerous individuals to secure wards
options.B: Promoting health and caring for mental alterations
options.C: Prescribing long-term psychotropic medications
options.D: Isolating patients from community stressors

explanation: As psychiatric nurses, our heart is in holistic care—helping patients build wellness, easing distress, and supporting them through tough emotional times.

question: A patient with a deep pressure ulcer is admitted to your ward. Why is increasing their protein intake so important for their care?

options.A: To cure any underlying bacterial pneumonia
options.B: To support collagen synthesis and tissue repair
options.C: To lower their overall daily caloric intake
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Wounds need raw materials to close up. Protein provides the building blocks (amino acids) needed to grow new skin and heal tissue.

question: What is a great way to help busy clinic staff keep data accurate without burning them out?

options.A: Eliminate all documentation requirements permanently across all clinics
options.B: Increase the number of complex indicators they must track every hour
options.C: Punish staff publicly every time a single tally mark is out of place
options.D: Keep data collection tools simple and provide ongoing training on their value

explanation: When nurses understand *why* data matters and have simple tools to record it, reporting becomes much easier and accurate!

question: Why might a patient having a severe gout flare still show a completely normal blood uric acid level on a lab test?

options.A: Blood tests are completely useless for diagnosing joint pain
options.B: Uric acid only travels through the urine, not the bloodstream
options.C: Blood tests cannot detect uric acid when a person is in pain
options.D: Uric acid can temporarily drop during an acute inflammation flare

explanation: Brilliant! During an actual flare, uric acid levels in the blood can dip down to normal ranges, meaning a blood test alone can sometimes play tricks on you.

question: Why does tertiary health care require much larger financial investments than primary care?

options.A: It requires expensive advanced technology and specialized equipment
options.B: It employs more administrative staff than clinical nurses
options.C: It only serves patients who pay cash upfront for services
options.D: It focuses exclusively on basic community health talks

explanation: Tertiary care deals with complex conditions requiring high-tech diagnostic and therapeutic machinery, which is very costly to buy and maintain. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check before starting AROM with a patient?

options.A: Force the patient's joints to bend rapidly.
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to the client.
options.C: Turn off all the lights in the patient room.
options.D: Check the medical record for specific joint restrictions.

explanation: Taking a quick look at the chart first ensures you don't accidentally work on a restricted or healing limb.

question: Why must you always place a weighing scale on a hard, flat surface before taking a reading?

options.A: To prevent the patient from feeling dizzy while standing
options.B: To protect the delicate internal electronic circuits from moisture
options.C: To make it easier for the nurse to read the digital screen
options.D: To ensure the weight distribution is even and the reading is accurate

explanation: Well done! Soft or uneven surfaces (like thick tiles with gaps or carpets) absorb pressure and mess up the scale's accuracy.

question: What is a major benefit of a junior nurse being mentored by an experienced researcher?

options.A: It allows the junior nurse to escape night shift duties permanently
options.B: It provides mentorship that demystifies publication and data analysis
options.C: It fulfills the legal requirement for hospital budget approval
options.D: It guarantees immediate international grants for the hospital

explanation: Mentorship is a game-changer! Having an experienced guide takes the fear out of research and shows you that publishing is totally doable.

question: What is a great quality to look for when picking members for a QI team?

options.A: Preference for keeping current hospital routines unchanged
options.B: High seniority status and administrative authority only
options.C: Curiosity about how things work and respect from peers
options.D: Experience working exclusively on the night shift

explanation: Spot on! Good team members need open minds to question old routines and enough respect from coworkers to get others on board.

question: Why is Vitamin K so effective at reversing the effects of warfarin?

options.A: It speeds up kidney filtration so warfarin leaves in the urine
options.B: It thickens the liquid plasma to stop bleeding instantly
options.C: It destroys the warfarin molecules floating in the blood
options.D: It bypasses the enzyme block to help the liver resume making clotting factors

explanation: Since warfarin blocks Vitamin K, giving extra Vitamin K gives the liver the exact ingredients it needs to get back to making clotting factors.

question: Which touch receptor is responsible for feeling deep pressure and fast vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Meissner corpuscles
options.C: Merkel discs
options.D: Ruffini endings

explanation: You nailed it! Pacinian corpuscles are large, deep receptors built specifically to catch rapid vibrations and heavy pressure.

question: How should community mental health nurses best approach traditional healers?

options.A: Through respectful dialogue and collaborative education
options.B: By threatening them with immediate police arrest
options.C: By ignoring their presence in the local community
options.D: By adopting all of their religious rituals into the hospital

explanation: Wonderful approach! Working alongside healers with mutual respect builds trust, making them much more likely to refer patients safely to formal hospitals.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to accessing social services for special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Severe financial hardship and poverty
options.B: Excessive availability of well-funded local rehabilitation centers
options.C: Infrastructural deficits and lack of accessible public buildings
options.D: Cultural stigma and negative beliefs about disability

explanation: Sadly, the real problem is a scarcity—not an excess—of well-funded rehabilitation centers in our communities.

question: A patient nods and says yes to everything you say while looking very confused. What should you do next?

options.A: Ask the patient to explain the instructions back in their own words
options.B: Write the instructions down and leave the room immediately
options.C: Speak much louder in case they have a hearing problem
options.D: Assume they understand because they agreed verbally

explanation: Using the teach-back method checks real understanding instead of relying on polite nods. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h2)

question: Why does a freshly mixed diluted lotion expire much faster than the original factory product?

options.A: Mixing breaks down preservatives and introduces potential microbes
options.B: The active drug evaporates completely within twenty-four hours
options.C: The packaging material reacts poorly to room lighting
options.D: Air pressure inside the room changes the chemical balance

explanation: Opening and mixing a product outside the factory opens the door to germs and weakens its built-in preservatives.

question: A patient with diabetes has a fasting blood sugar of 55 mg/dL and is shaky and confused. What is the most likely cause of these symptoms?

options.A: Kidney failure causing a backup of metabolic waste
options.B: A normal reaction to an overnight fasting period
options.C: Dehydration from drinking too much plain water
options.D: Brain glucose deprivation from low blood sugar

explanation: When blood sugar drops too low, the brain lacks energy, causing neurological symptoms like confusion and shaking. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the main difference between a primary and a secondary skin lesion?

options.A: Secondary lesions are always malignant, whereas primary ones are benign
options.B: Primary lesions contain fluid, while secondary lesions are strictly solid
options.C: Primary lesions only appear on the face, while secondary ones appear on limbs
options.D: Secondary lesions evolve from primary lesions due to scratching or healing

explanation: Primary lesions show up first on healthy skin. Secondary ones form later because of things like scratching, picking, or the natural healing process.

question: How is putting a catheter into a male patient different from a female patient?

options.A: It lacks a sphincter muscle, making insertion completely effortless
options.B: It opens directly into the abdominal cavity
options.C: It is longer and has natural curves that require careful maneuvering
options.D: It is wider, requiring much larger catheter sizes

explanation: Exactly! The male urethra is longer and travels through the prostate, so you have to gently navigate a few natural bends during the procedure.

question: Why must a patient with liver cirrhosis watch their daily sodium intake?

options.A: To prevent fluid from pooling in the abdominal cavity
options.B: To prevent painful muscle cramps in the legs
options.C: To encourage rapid absorption of dietary iron
options.D: To stop sudden spikes in blood glucose levels

explanation: Spot on! Liver issues can cause fluid to collect in the belly (ascites), and eating too much salt makes this swelling much worse.

question: Why is teaching new staff about infection control only on their first day not enough?

options.A: Hospital management changes policies every single week without fail
options.B: New nurses never listen to instructions given on their first day
options.C: Good habits fade and new safety guidelines emerge over time
options.D: Trainees are not allowed to touch patients until their second year

explanation: You got it! Regular refreshers keep safety fresh in everyone's mind as new guidelines come out.

question: A patient arrives with a severe insect sting on their hand, and the hand is swelling up massively. What quick check should you do next?

options.A: Draw blood samples for comprehensive metabolic panels
options.B: Check distal pulses, movement, and sensation in the fingers
options.C: Measure the patient's exact height and weight
options.D: Prepare the patient for immediate surgical amputation

explanation: When a tight space like the hand swells up, blood flow and nerves can get squeezed. Checking fingers for pulses, feeling, and movement helps catch bad circulation early!

question: How can market-driven hospital policies directly impact bedside nursing practice?

options.A: By prioritizing fast patient turnover and tight staffing ratios
options.B: By eliminating all administrative paperwork duties
options.C: By ensuring nurses control hospital budgets
options.D: By guaranteeing unlimited time for patient education

explanation: Corporate models focus on efficiency and cost reduction, which often translates to leaner staffing and faster discharges. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care once a patient enters the active dying phase?

options.A: Checking blood pressure and pulse every fifteen minutes
options.B: Trying to restart vital signs with emergency medications
options.C: Ensuring absolute comfort and supporting the family
options.D: Forcing fluids by mouth to stop dehydration

explanation: When active dying begins, our focus shifts completely from trying to cure to keeping the patient comfortable and wrapping the family in support. You are doing amazing!

question: A patient with chronic bowel inflammation passes pale, bulky, foul-smelling stools that float. What nutritional problem does this suggest?

options.A: Fat malabsorption due to impaired intestinal function.
options.B: A sudden increase in stomach acid production.
options.C: Excessive intake of dietary fiber and green vegetables.
options.D: Rapid dehydration caused by drinking too little water.

explanation: Pale, bulky, and foul-smelling stools that float indicate steatorrhea, which means fats are not being absorbed properly in the gut. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h4)

question: A stroke patient is trying to stick out their tongue, but it keeps pulling to one side. Which muscle is likely affected?

options.A: Palatoglossus
options.B: Hyoglossus
options.C: Genioglossus
options.D: Styloglossus

explanation: The genioglossus is our main tongue-poking muscle! When one side gets weak after a stroke, the tongue deviates toward the weaker side.

question: A patient with a blood pressure of 220/130 mmHg complains of a sudden, blinding headache and confusion. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink a large glass of salty broth.
options.B: Wait two hours to see if the headache goes away on its own.
options.C: Tell the patient to lie down and sleep it off until morning.
options.D: Arrange emergency transport to a hospital immediately.

explanation: Severe blood pressure elevation accompanied by neurological symptoms indicates a hypertensive emergency requiring urgent medical intervention. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h6)

question: Why do we have formal research guidelines like the Belmont Report in healthcare?

options.A: To help hospitals make more money
options.B: To prevent exploitation and protect human participants from harm
options.C: To guarantee positive study results
options.D: To speed up drug approvals

explanation: Exactly! Past abuses taught us that research participants need strong, guaranteed protection for their safety and rights.

question: Why does good teamwork improve a patient's transition from the hospital to home?

options.A: Different team members coordinate discharge education and resources smoothly
options.B: Doctors make all final decisions without consulting family members
options.C: Patients are discharged much faster without receiving any medications
options.D: Nurses take over all financial responsibilities for the household

explanation: You nailed it! Smooth teamwork ensures that when a patient is ready to go home, everyone (nurses, doctors, pharmacists, social workers) is on the same page.

question: A nurse is getting ready for surgery and notices a fresh scratch on the back of her hand. What should she do?

options.A: Rub antiseptic over it and wear double gloves
options.B: Report the scratch and take on a non-sterile role
options.C: Scrub for a longer time using special soap
options.D: Cover it tightly with a waterproof plaster and go ahead

explanation: Safety first! Open cuts let bacteria escape into the sterile field, so it's best to step back and take a non-sterile duty.

question: Which payment setup best promotes true equity in a health system?

options.A: Progressive prepayment systems where wealthier individuals contribute more to fund care for everyone
options.B: Relying entirely on patient donations collected inside hospital waiting rooms
options.C: Strict out-of-pocket user fees charged at the hospital door for every single service
options.D: Flat-rate private insurance premiums that cost the same for low- and high-income earners

explanation: When those who earn more chip in a bit extra, it helps protect and cover those who have less. That's true fairness!

question: How does the work differ between a Senior CHEW and a Junior CHEW?

options.A: Junior CHEWs perform major surgeries, while Seniors only do paperwork
options.B: Senior CHEWs only work in cities, while Juniors work exclusively abroad
options.C: Senior CHEWs handle independent diagnoses and treatments under protocol, while Juniors work under closer supervision
options.D: There is no difference in their training or daily clinical duties

explanation: You got it! Senior CHEWs have extra training that lets them manage common health issues independently using standing orders, while juniors work more closely with supervisors.

question: What is a major direct benefit of having a strong, positive nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Removal of the need for professional nursing documentation
options.B: Complete elimination of all chronic diseases in society
options.C: Fewer emergency hospital readmissions and better adherence
options.D: Higher medical bills for the patient and household

explanation: Brilliant! When patients trust their nurse, they follow their care plan better, stay healthier at home, and avoid sudden trips back to the hospital.

question: How does political interference usually affect public health spending in Nigeria?

options.A: Projects are sometimes placed where politicians want rather than where health needs are greatest
options.B: Corruption is completely eradicated from hospital boards
options.C: Budgets are automatically increased to match international health targets
options.D: Hospitals receive surplus medical equipment in every rural ward

explanation: Sometimes health facilities are built to score political points in certain areas rather than going where the actual health data shows they are needed.

question: A nursing researcher wants to mark down the exact presence or absence of hand hygiene steps among ward staff during a shift. Which tool should they use?

options.A: Audio recording
options.B: Checklist
options.C: Unstructured narrative
options.D: Rating scale

explanation: Checklists are ideal for recording whether specific, distinct actions occurred or did not occur. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h3)

question: Why is emotional support and clear teaching so important for patients undergoing tests for blood disorders?

options.A: Kind words replace the need for local numbing medicine
options.B: Patients must memorize all lab ranges before going home
options.C: Clear explanations keep the lab machines from breaking down
options.D: The tests often look for serious illnesses like cancer, which causes high worry

explanation: Waiting for results on serious conditions can be terrifying. Your gentle reassurance and clear explanations make a world of difference for a worried patient.

question: Which of these is NOT a major long-term complication of uncontrolled high blood pressure?

options.A: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Chronic kidney disease
options.C: Stroke
options.D: Myocardial infarction

explanation: Correct! Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition involving the pancreas, not something directly caused by high blood pressure.

question: What is the main purpose of using the SBAR communication tool in the ward?

options.A: Punishing nurses who fail to document vital signs on time
options.B: Ensuring hospital administrators can track the exact location of staff
options.C: Replacing all written patient care charts with audio recordings
options.D: Providing a clear, standardized script to share critical patient data

explanation: SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) gives you a quick, reliable script so you can pass on vital patient info clearly and without panic.

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing a severely injured teenager in the emergency unit?

options.A: Securing the airway and stabilizing breathing
options.B: Calling the legal authorities for documentation
options.C: Asking about the history of the quarrel
options.D: Administering long-term psychiatric counseling

explanation: You got it! In emergency trauma care, the primary survey always comes first—focusing on airway, breathing, and circulation to keep the patient alive.

question: What happens if a researcher doesn't clearly define an abstract idea like anxiety in their study?

options.A: The study becomes completely free of bias
options.B: The hospital automatically receives more research funding
options.C: Study results become hard to compare across different populations
options.D: Patients stop feeling anxious during procedures

explanation: Spot on! If everyone defines a term differently, it's impossible to fairly compare the results or repeat the study elsewhere.

question: Besides physical changes, what major personal transformation happens during pregnancy?

options.A: Immediate social isolation
options.B: Permanent cognitive decline
options.C: Profound psychological journey
options.D: Complete personality replacement

explanation: You've got this! Pregnancy is as much an emotional and psychological adjustment as it is a physical one. Moms are processing a whole new identity!

question: What is the main purpose of a feedback slip in the referral process?

options.A: To notify the primary clinic about the outcome of the client's visit
options.B: To order new contraceptive commodities from the central medical store
options.C: To serve as a receipt for hospital treatment fees paid by the client
options.D: To record the daily attendance of nurses at the tertiary hospital

explanation: The feedback slip is like a reply letter! It travels back from the big hospital to tell your clinic what treatment was given.

question: What does indirect calorimetry measure to calculate energy use?

options.A: Urinary nitrogen and fluid loss
options.B: Total body heat in a sealed room
options.C: Oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production
options.D: Electrical resistance of skin tissue

explanation: Spot on! Indirect calorimetry figures out how many calories someone is burning by analyzing the gases they breathe in and out.

question: What health issue do we frequently see in children with heavy gut parasite infections?

options.A: High blood pressure and stroke
options.B: Sudden bone fractures
options.C: Malnutrition and anemia
options.D: Rapid hair loss and blindness

explanation: Parasites steal nutrients and blood from the host, which often leads to poor growth and anemia in young ones. You nailed it!

question: Why do modern nursing guidelines usually discourage using traditional circular air rings (doughnut cushions)?

options.A: The rim can cut off blood flow and worsen tissue damage
options.B: They are too expensive to clean and disinfect between patients
options.C: They make it impossible to adjust the hospital bed height
options.D: They trap excessive moisture and cause fungal infections

explanation: That's right! The hard edges of a doughnut cushion squeeze surrounding tiny blood vessels, cutting off circulation and actually increasing the risk of pressure sores.

question: Why would an educator use parallel forms reliability for a student exam?

options.A: To eliminate the need for statistical software like SPSS during analysis
options.B: To ensure patients do not experience physical fatigue during long interviews
options.C: To prevent students from copying answers by using two equivalent test versions
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of printing paper questionnaires in the hospital

explanation: Having two fair, equivalent versions of a test lets you switch up questions between rows in a crowded hall without sacrificing test quality!

question: In which section of the fallopian tube does fertilization usually occur?

options.A: Ampulla
options.B: Fimbriae
options.C: Isthmus
options.D: Cervix

explanation: The ampulla is the wide middle section where sperm and egg typically meet and fertilize. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h4)

question: What does morbidity measure in a community?

options.A: The state of being unhealthy or diseased
options.B: The total number of registered deaths
options.C: The number of new babies born in a year
options.D: The amount of money earned by hospitals

explanation: Morbidity focuses on illness, sickness, and disease prevalence rather than death itself. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why doesn't the mother's immune system attack and reject the fetus as a foreign body?

options.A: The syncytiotrophoblast lacks the usual antigens that trigger immune rejection
options.B: Fetal blood cells destroy any maternal immune cells that enter the cord
options.C: The amniotic fluid contains strong chemicals that destroy antibodies
options.D: The mother stops producing white blood cells entirely during pregnancy

explanation: The outer surface of the placenta (syncytiotrophoblast) cleverly hides from the mother's immune system by not showing the usual markers that trigger rejection. Immunology at its finest! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h7)

question: When should a nurse ideally start rehab care for a hospitalized patient?

options.A: As soon as the patient is medically stable
options.B: After the patient is completely discharged home
options.C: When the family requests assistance with daily tasks
options.D: Only when all physical therapy orders are finished

explanation: Great thinking! Starting early stops stiff joints and weak muscles before they even start.

question: During a reproductive review of systems, which symptom is a red flag that needs a closer look?

options.A: Eating three balanced meals every day
options.B: Unexplained abnormal vaginal discharge or odor
options.C: A normal resting heart rate
options.D: Sleeping eight hours every night

explanation: Unusual discharge or smells are often the body's way of signaling an infection or irritation in the reproductive tract that needs treatment.

question: Which environmental issue is currently one of the biggest threats to farming and food supplies?

options.A: Strict government food safety regulations
options.B: Decreased global demand for fresh vegetables
options.C: Excessive use of indoor community gardens
options.D: Climate change and erratic weather patterns

explanation: Unpredictable rains, extreme droughts, and severe floods ruin crops globally, making it harder for farmers to keep up food production.

question: What is the main focus of Behavioral Change Communication (BCC) in nutrition?

options.A: Addressing cultural habits and beliefs influencing food choices
options.B: Importing expensive nutritional supplements from abroad
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties for poor dietary habits
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests on food chemical safety

explanation: That's right! BCC looks past simple facts to understand the cultural and social reasons behind how people choose and prepare their meals.

question: Why is it risky for a nursing research project to lack clear objectives?

options.A: The study will easily lose direction and gather irrelevant data
options.B: The nursing staff will refuse to participate in the study
options.C: The sample size will become too large to calculate
options.D: The hospital ethics committee will automatically grant funding

explanation: Without clear targets, you might end up collecting a mountain of unnecessary information that doesn't actually solve your clinical problem. Good objectives keep you focused! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the fastest, most effective way to stop severe bleeding on a patient's arm or leg?

options.A: Give them water to drink to replace lost blood
options.B: Lift the legs up high
options.C: Apply direct pressure or a tourniquet
options.D: Apply ice packs directly to the wound

explanation: Well done! Direct pressure or a tourniquet squeezes those bleeding vessels shut and stops dangerous blood loss fast.

question: What is the safest way for a new mother to clean her perineal area after using the toilet?

options.A: Soaking in soapy bathwater
options.B: Washing from back to front
options.C: Washing from front to back
options.D: Wiping vigorously with dry paper

explanation: Front to back always! This golden rule keeps germs from the anal area away from the vagina and urethra, protecting her from nasty infections.

question: What is the safest way to check if a patient has drug allergies before giving a medication?

options.A: Trust that the pharmacy filtered out all possible allergens
options.B: Ask a family member if the patient has any food preferences
options.C: Check the chart, look at the allergy band, and ask the patient directly
options.D: Review only the physical allergy band on the bed frame

explanation: Using multiple checks like the chart, band, and talking to the patient ensures nothing gets missed. You've got this!

question: What is the main reason nurses use the Barthel Index assessment tool?

options.A: To diagnose the primary neurological cause of paralysis
options.B: To measure a patient's independence in activities of daily living
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity
options.D: To calculate the exact dosage of pain medication needed

explanation: The Barthel Index is simply a helpful scoring guide to see how well a patient can handle basic tasks like eating, washing, and moving around.

question: What was the main goal of introducing workers' compensation laws?

options.A: To fund free medical schools for aspiring occupational health nurses
options.B: To allow employers to fire injured workers immediately without paying severance
options.C: To punish factory owners by throwing them in prison for safety violations
options.D: To provide financial support for workers injured on the job without requiring lawsuits

explanation: Workers' comp ensured that staff hurt on the job got medical care and money for bills without having to go through stressful court battles.

question: A rural clinic lacks basic drugs and staff because government funds are delayed. What is the biggest immediate risk to patients?

options.A: Being overcharged by government health insurance schemes
options.B: Receiving free specialized surgeries at the local facility
options.C: Avoiding needed care or experiencing worsened health conditions
options.D: Enjoying excess medication supplies stored in the pharmacy

explanation: When clinics are empty and unfunded, sick people stay home, delay getting help, and unfortunately risk getting much worse.

question: What does the intravenous route involve delivering substances directly into?

options.A: Muscle tissue for slow absorption
options.B: Fatty tissue beneath the skin
options.C: Systemic circulation through a vein
options.D: The digestive tract via the stomach

explanation: Intravenous means inside a vein, allowing direct delivery into the bloodstream for rapid effect. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why are teenagers often more prone to screen addiction than older adults?

options.A: Their prefrontal cortex is still maturing, making impulse control difficult
options.B: They have more financial resources to purchase high-end gadgets
options.C: They spend less time sleeping than adults do on average
options.D: Their eyes are more sensitive to the blue light emitted by screens

explanation: Think about brain development! The part of the brain that helps with self-control and good judgment is still growing in teens, making it harder to put the phone down.

question: Why do pregnant women in vulnerable homes face a higher risk of severe delivery complications?

options.A: Government rules stop them from visiting clinics
options.B: They often lack transport money and funds for professional care
options.C: Pregnancy problems only happen in city slums
options.D: Traditional birth attendants are always safer than hospitals

explanation: Right! Money issues and transport delays often prevent vulnerable mothers from getting skilled help during emergencies.

question: What is zero-based budgeting?

options.A: Cutting all nursing salaries down to zero during a financial crisis
options.B: Simply adding five percent to whatever was spent last year
options.C: Requiring departments to justify all expenses from scratch every year
options.D: Operating the hospital with zero money until donations arrive

explanation: Zero-based budgeting forces managers to prove the value of every single cost rather than just copying the previous year. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is a major risk factor to look for when assessing family caregivers of a neurologic client?

options.A: Having too many relatives visiting the hospital
options.B: Asking nurses too many questions about medications
options.C: Buying extra blankets for the client's bed
options.D: Caregiver burnout and physical exhaustion

explanation: Caregivers often neglect their own health, leading to exhaustion that threatens the sustainability of home care. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h6)

question: How does severe obesity negatively impact male reproductive health?

options.A: Obesity stops the pituitary gland from ever producing luteinizing hormone
options.B: Body fat physically blocks sperm from leaving the epididymis during ejaculation
options.C: Adipose cells directly attack mature sperm cells in the seminal fluid
options.D: Fat tissue converts extra testosterone into estrogen, disrupting the hormonal balance

explanation: Fatty tissue contains aromatase, an enzyme that turns testosterone into estrogen, which interferes with normal sperm creation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: Why must Nigerian nurses always check the NAFDAC number on drug packaging?

options.A: To calculate the precise half-life of the drug in the patient's bloodstream
options.B: To find out which pharmaceutical company holds the international trade patent
options.C: To confirm the product is legally approved and guard against fake or substandard drugs
options.D: To determine the exact chemical formula of the active ingredient
