options.C: Give all prescription drugs immediately
options.D: Gather laboratory test results first

explanation: Correct! Good nursing care starts with a warm welcome to put the client at ease and build a trusting relationship.

question: What happens when the internal urethral sphincter relaxes during normal urination?

options.A: The kidneys immediately start producing a fresh batch of urine.
options.B: Semen is forced backward into the bladder instead of moving forward.
options.C: The pelvic floor muscles contract violently to push out the remaining waste.
options.D: Urine is allowed to flow out of the bladder into the upper urethra.

explanation: Spot on! Relaxing this internal muscle opens the bladder neck so urine can begin its journey down.

question: Why can diagnosing an emerging infection be very difficult during the early stages?

options.A: Patients refuse to answer basic questions about their health
options.B: Laboratory equipment automatically destroys new viral samples
options.C: Early symptoms often look identical to common endemic illnesses
options.D: Fever never appears during the first week of any infection

explanation: Initial signs like fever, headache, and body aches are shared by many everyday diseases, making unique identification tricky at first. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h5)

question: Where is milk actually manufactured inside the breast?

options.A: Nipple pores
options.B: Adipose cells
options.C: Areola glands
options.D: Alveoli

explanation: Alveoli are tiny, hollow sacs lined with milk-secreting cells where lactation actually takes place. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h4)

question: What is the medical term for pale, greasy, and very foul-smelling stools caused by fats that weren't absorbed?

options.A: Melena
options.B: Glycosuria
options.C: Hematochezia
options.D: Steatorrhea

explanation: When fats escape digestion and absorption, they show up in the waste, giving stool that classic pale, oily, and heavy-smelling look known as steatorrhea.

question: Which of these statements about emergency contraception pills is FALSE?

options.A: They are most effective when taken soon after intercourse
options.B: They work by delaying the release of an egg from the ovary
options.C: They cause permanent and irreversible infertility in women
options.D: They do not protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Emergency pills do NOT make a woman barren! Their hormonal effect is short-term and has zero effect on future fertility. Busting myths like a pro!

question: A nurse is accidentally poked by a needle from a patient who has Hepatitis B. Why is this exposure especially scary?

options.A: Hepatitis B spreads easily through casual air contact in the room.
options.B: There are no post-exposure vaccines or treatments available for Hepatitis B.
options.C: Hepatitis B has the highest transmission risk per exposure among common bloodborne viruses.
options.D: Hepatitis B can instantly destroy human skin cells on contact.

explanation: Compared to HIV or Hepatitis C, Hepatitis B is much more infectious. A single contaminated prick has a very high chance of passing the virus on if you aren't vaccinated.

question: What is the primary function of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To catch and guide the released egg into the tube
options.B: To propel sperm upward toward the uterine cavity
options.C: To produce the hormones estrogen and progesterone
options.D: To provide structural support to the lower abdomen

explanation: The fimbriae are finger-like projections that sweep over the ovary surface during ovulation to catch the newly released egg and draw it inside. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h2)

question: What is the main goal of doing a review of systems during an interview?

options.A: To perform a complete hands-on physical examination
options.B: To diagnose every chronic disease the patient has
options.C: To test the patient's knowledge of anatomy and physiology
options.D: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or omitted

explanation: You got it! The review of systems acts as a helpful safety net to catch any symptoms the patient forgot to mention.

question: A client comes to the clinic reporting pus, warmth, and increasing redness around her implant site five days after placement. What should you suspect?

options.A: A localized site infection requiring prompt medical evaluation and treatment
options.B: A sign that the implant has expired and needs immediate replacement
options.C: A normal healing reaction that proves the hormone is working effectively
options.D: A standard allergic reaction to the pressure bandage adhesive tape

explanation: Pus, warmth, and spreading redness are classic signs of a minor wound infection. It's nothing to panic about, but it definitely needs prompt cleaning and medical care!

question: A nurse in a busy Lagos clinic wants to cut down patient waiting times without buying new computers. What is the best approach?

options.A: Complain to the patients about the lack of staff instead of changing anything
options.B: Refuse to see any patients who arrive after eight o'clock in the morning
options.C: Use a PDSA cycle to test reorganizing the patient triage and record-pulling process
options.D: Wait until the government donates brand new digital tablets to the clinic

explanation: You nailed it! Reorganizing how we do things using a quick PDSA test is a fantastic way to improve patient flow without spending money.

question: Why can it be risky to rely only on your eyes and nose to check if food is safe?

options.A: Good bacteria always smell worse than dangerous bacteria
options.B: All spoiled foods look and smell completely normal until cooked
options.C: Some harmful pathogens cause no visible change in taste, smell, or appearance
options.D: Human taste buds cannot detect any form of microbial waste

explanation: This is a classic trap! Dangerous bacteria don't always change how food looks, smells, or tastes, which is why safe handling is always a must.

question: If a patient loses their sense of taste on the front two-thirds of their tongue after ear surgery, which nerve was likely nudged?

options.A: Lingual nerve
options.B: Glossopharyngeal nerve
options.C: Chorda tympani nerve
options.D: Hypoglossal nerve

explanation: The chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve carries taste messages from the front of the tongue and happens to run right through the middle ear.

question: How is a nursing audit different from a general staff performance appraisal?

options.A: Audits are done only by doctors, while appraisals are done by senior nurses
options.B: Audits deal with hospital finances, while appraisals deal with patient beds
options.C: Audits happen daily, while appraisals happen only once in a lifetime
options.D: Audits focus on patient care processes, while appraisals focus on overall staff conduct

explanation: Great thinking! A performance appraisal looks at how a nurse behaves on the job overall, while an audit zooms in specifically on clinical care and nursing records.

question: A client looks very scared about going to the general hospital to remove a contraceptive implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Cancel the referral and send the client home without protection
options.B: Scold the client for being afraid of a minor procedure
options.C: Tell her that hospitals are terrifying places and she must just endure it
options.D: Listen to her concerns, explain the procedure simply, and reassure her

explanation: Fear is completely normal. Sitting down to listen and breaking down what will happen turns anxiety into confidence.

question: What usually causes an AED to flash a 'Check Pads' error message?

options.A: The patient's heart rate is too fast for the machine to read
options.B: The rescuer is pressing the shock button at the wrong time
options.C: Loose cable connections or moisture on the patient's skin
options.D: The battery inside the computer unit is completely dead

explanation: If pads aren't sticking well or the skin is wet, the machine can't get a good connection. A quick dry and press usually fixes it!

question: A patient feels heavy, has aching muscles, and can't sleep well—yet tests show no physical disease. What matches this?

options.A: Bacterial meningitis
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Neurasthenia

explanation: Brilliant! When physical weakness and poor sleep won't go away and tests are clear, it points straight to neurasthenia. You're doing awesome.

question: What is the purpose of binding the chest with cloth after applying heat during breast ironing?

options.A: To hold medicinal herbal leaves in place
options.B: To absorb sweat from the heated stones
options.C: To keep the chest warm during cold weather
options.D: To physically restrict future breast growth

explanation: Tight binding is used alongside heat to prevent the breast tissue from expanding outward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is the main feature of a capital cost?

options.A: It involves a large investment in long-term assets
options.B: It changes every time a single patient is admitted
options.C: It covers minor daily items like cleaning supplies
options.D: It must be paid in cash at the end of every shift

explanation: Capital costs are big-ticket investments—like buying a new building or heavy machinery—that stay with the hospital for years.

question: How do long-term high food prices contribute to chronic illnesses like diabetes and obesity in vulnerable communities?

options.A: By eliminating the body's natural ability to process natural sugars
options.B: By forcing families to rely heavily on cheap, highly processed, carbohydrate-heavy foods
options.C: By providing extra financial funds for families to buy excessive amounts of meat
options.D: By encouraging children to exercise less due to high grocery store bills

explanation: When healthy food becomes too expensive, families buy cheap processed items that lack nutrition and promote chronic disease. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h8)

question: Why is knowing the stages of the Transtheoretical Model useful for a clinical nurse?

options.A: It accurately predicts the exact day a patient will stop smoking or exercising
options.B: It helps tailor counselling to match the patient's exact readiness to change
options.C: It proves whether a patient has a genetic predisposition to chronic illness
options.D: It replaces the need for physical assessments during routine clinic visits

explanation: Exactly right! People change at their own pace. Knowing their stage helps you meet them where they are instead of pushing too hard too fast.

question: What is a conflict of interest in a research study?

options.A: When the researchers forget to write an abstract for the paper
options.B: When two nurses disagree on how to make a bed
options.C: When the hospital library runs out of nursing journals
options.D: When the study funders stand to gain financially from positive results

explanation: Financial or professional ties to a product being tested can introduce bias into how a study is conducted or reported. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h5)

question: How do vocational and peer support programs help a patient newly released on parole?

options.A: They completely replace the need for antipsychotic medications.
options.B: They rebuild daily routines, confidence, and social connections.
options.C: They guarantee that the patient will never feel stressed again.
options.D: They allow the legal system to close the patient's case file forever.

explanation: You got it! Healing goes beyond just stopping symptoms; patients need help rebuilding their confidence, daily habits, and friendships.

question: What happens to the body when someone goes without sleep for too long?

options.A: Sensory processing becomes sharper
options.B: Muscle mass grows automatically
options.C: Immune function becomes compromised
options.D: Metabolic rate permanently increases

explanation: Missing sleep puts stress on your body and wears down your immune defenses. Remember to get some rest during exam prep week!

question: A patient scheduled for a CT scan with contrast says they have a severe allergy to shellfish. What should you do first?

options.A: Proceed with the scan because shellfish has no link to dye
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink extra water for one hour
options.C: Administer an oral dose of calcium supplements right away
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately before the test

explanation: Shellfish allergies often overlap with iodine-based contrast allergies. Always alert the doctor right away so they can order premedication or choose a safer option.

question: Which type of drug molecule is most likely to leave the body through the biliary system (bile) rather than the kidneys?

options.A: Tiny, water-soluble molecules
options.B: Large, fat-soluble compounds
options.C: Strongly ionized electrolytes
options.D: Volatile inhaled gases

explanation: Remember: small water-soluble molecules love going out through the kidneys, while the biliary system prefers larger, fat-soluble compounds!

question: Why do voluntary agencies often include counseling in programs for stigmatized illnesses?

options.A: To replace the need for laboratory blood tests
options.B: To help patients cope with emotional distress and social stigma
options.C: To gather evidence for criminal court prosecutions
options.D: To force patients to relocate to urban cities

explanation: You nailed it. Illnesses like HIV or tuberculosis come with heavy emotional weight; counseling gives patients the mental strength to keep taking their treatment.

question: Which of these is NOT a physical danger faced by waste handlers in the hospital?

options.A: Potential infection from contaminated biological specimens
options.B: Routine promotion to hospital management positions
options.C: Accidental needle-stick injuries during linen sorting
options.D: Direct exposure to toxic chemical fumes from burning plastics

explanation: That's right! A promotion is a career win, not a workplace hazard. Handlers face real physical risks like injuries and toxic fumes.

question: What is the official paper form that Nigerian health workers use to report adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Blue Card Sheet
options.B: Yellow Form
options.C: Red Discharge Tag
options.D: Green Admission Book

explanation: Whenever you spot a nasty drug reaction in practice, grab the NAFDAC Yellow Form and report it!

question: How can a nurse manager protect their decision-making process from personal mental biases?

options.A: Make all important administrative choices in absolute secrecy
options.B: Avoid gathering any data to keep the mind completely clear
options.C: Actively consult diverse team members and check objective data
options.D: Trust gut feelings completely without listening to anyone else

explanation: Getting input from your team and looking at hard facts is the best way to burst through personal blind spots!

question: Why shouldn't you use a strong hospital surface disinfectant on an open wound?

options.A: It will cause severe chemical burns and damage the living tissue.
options.B: It will make the bacteria grow faster inside the wound.
options.C: It will change the color of the patient's skin permanently.
options.D: It will wash away the local anesthetic effects.

explanation: You got it! Disinfectants are way too strong for human cells. They would destroy healthy tissue along with the germs, causing serious injury.

question: What is a likely consequence of poor communication among home health team members?

options.A: Conflicting instructions given to the patient and family
options.B: Reduced need for interprofessional documentation
options.C: Better alignment between nursing and therapy goals
options.D: Faster recovery times due to independent decision-making

explanation: When team members fail to communicate, patients and caregivers may receive mixed guidance, leading to confusion and safety risks. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h6)

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

options.A: Frequent requests for promotion and salary increases
options.B: Sudden weight loss, hair discoloration, and chronic joint pain
options.C: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment
options.D: Excessive enthusiasm, overconfidence, and skipping breaks

explanation: Burnout makes you feel emotionally drained, detached from patients, and like nothing you do makes a difference. Always check on your mental health!

question: What does the FEFO inventory rule stand for in vaccine management?

options.A: Fastest Entry, Fastest Out
options.B: First Expire, First Out
options.C: Freeze Early, Freeze Often
options.D: Final Evaluation, Final Order

explanation: FEFO ensures that vaccines nearing their expiration date are used before newer supplies to prevent wastage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: What should a nurse do when family members demand full resuscitation, but the patient has a valid, documented DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) order?

options.A: Call the police immediately to remove the family
options.B: Hide the medical chart so the family cannot see it
options.C: Ignore the DNR and follow the family's verbal demands
options.D: Uphold the patient's documented wishes while providing compassionate support to the family

explanation: The patient's legally documented wishes always come first. At the same time, we support the grieving family with empathy and clear communication. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h5)

question: Why is long-term sustainability such an important goal for community health programs?

options.A: It guarantees that nurses will receive permanent salary increases from the state
options.B: It ensures health promotion continues after external project funding eventually stops
options.C: It prevents infectious disease outbreaks from occurring in urban slums
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for future community health assessments

explanation: Spot on! External grants and projects eventually end. Building local community leadership ensures that the good work keeps going long after outsiders leave.

question: How does a negative pressure isolation room stop airborne diseases from escaping?

options.A: It draws air into the room and stops it from escaping into the hallway
options.B: It raises the room temperature to kill suspended viral particles
options.C: It pushes clean air outward into the public hospital corridors
options.D: It creates a vacuum that destroys bacteria before they multiply

explanation: You nailed it! Think of it like a gentle draft pulling inward; when the door opens, air rushes inside rather than letting contaminated room air leak out into the hall.

question: How does listening to patient and family feedback help nurses improve the ward?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for scientific research articles
options.B: It allows nurses to spend less time documenting patient charts
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will receive increased government funding
options.D: It reveals gaps in care that clinical staff might easily overlook

explanation: Patients experience the hospital from a totally different angle. Their feedback helps us catch little things we might miss while rushing through our busy shifts.

question: Why must patients with liver disease avoid taking casual painkillers like paracetamol without asking a doctor?

options.A: It neutralizes the effects of prescribed lactulose syrup
options.B: The liver has to process it, and it can cause more damage
options.C: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in liver patients
options.D: It increases the risk of dehydration and kidney failure

explanation: Medications like paracetamol are processed by the liver. When the liver is weak, these drugs can build up quickly and cause serious harm.

question: A psychiatric nurse is caring for someone starting a new antipsychotic medication. What is a key nursing duty here?

options.A: Assuming the medication will cure the social crisis causing the illness
options.B: Telling the patient to stop taking the drug if they feel slightly tired
options.C: Monitoring for medication side effects and educating the family on adherence
options.D: Limiting therapy sessions strictly to once a decade

explanation: As a nurse, watching out for side effects and making sure the patient and family understand how to take the drugs safely is a core part of your job!

question: Which type of abuse involves controlling money and financial resources to keep power over a partner?

options.A: Psychological abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Physical abuse
options.D: Sexual abuse

explanation: Economic abuse traps people by cutting them off from money, jobs, and financial freedom. Spotting this helps us understand the full picture of abuse.

question: When a registered nurse delegates a task to a junior worker, what happens to the ultimate accountability for that patient's care?

options.A: It transfers completely to the healthcare worker who performs the task
options.B: It remains with the registered nurse who delegated the task
options.C: It is shared equally between the hospital management and the worker
options.D: It dissolves once the task is completed and documented

explanation: Remember this golden nursing rule: you can delegate tasks, but the ultimate accountability for patient care always stays with the Registered Nurse!

question: Why is looking into a patient's eye with an ophthalmoscope so useful for checking whole-body health?

options.A: The eye mirrors the brain with 100% perfection
options.B: It lets doctors look directly at living tiny blood vessels and nerves
options.C: It is the only organ affected by high blood sugar
options.D: It has the most pain receptors in the body

explanation: Spot on! Because the eye is clear, healthcare workers can peer right inside to see how tiny blood vessels are doing without cutting anything open.

question: Why do we grab a cold pack immediately after someone suffers a fresh joint sprain?

options.A: To heat up the deep tissue and relax tight tendons
options.B: To stimulate rapid cell division in the bone
options.C: To dilate vessels and increase local bleeding
options.D: To constrict blood vessels and reduce swelling

explanation: Spot on! Cold causes vasoconstriction (narrowing the vessels), which slows down blood flow to the fresh injury so it doesn't blow up into a huge swelling.

question: For how many months should an infant be exclusively breastfed (no other food or water)?

options.A: First three months
options.B: First six months
options.C: First twelve months
options.D: First two weeks

explanation: Correct! Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives a baby all the food and immune defense they need without needing water or other foods yet.

question: Through which part of the spinal cord do outgoing motor signals leave?

options.A: Dorsal root
options.B: Dorsal root ganglion
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: While sensory signals enter through the dorsal side, motor instructions head out to the muscles through the ventral root at the front.

question: What do we call single-ring sugar molecules like glucose and fructose?

options.A: Amino acids
options.B: Monosaccharides
options.C: Polysaccharides
options.D: Triglycerides

explanation: You got it! 'Mono' means single, and 'saccharide' means sugar, making monosaccharides the simplest form of carbohydrate.

question: What is a major cause of strain on traditional family elder care systems in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory government placement of all seniors into nursing homes
options.B: A complete cultural loss of respect for older family members
options.C: Urbanization and the migration of younger relatives to cities
options.D: The total absence of any chronic health conditions in the elderly

explanation: As younger family members move to urban centers for work, the traditional extended family network available at home to care for elders is stretched thin. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h7)

question: How does involving local residents in a community diagnosis help public health programs?

options.A: It builds local ownership and cooperation for the health programs
options.B: It shifts all financial responsibility entirely onto the villagers
options.C: It ensures that no diseases will ever reappear in the community
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to collect any data themselves

explanation: Spot on! When community members are part of identifying their challenges, they are much more willing to embrace and support the solutions.

question: What is the name of the tough, outermost layer of the meninges?

options.A: Choroid plexus
options.B: Dura mater
options.C: Arachnoid mater
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: The dura mater is the tough, fibrous outermost protective layer covering the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is another common name for primary polycythaemia?

options.A: Polycythaemia vera
options.B: Secondary erythrocytosis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Aplastic anemia

explanation: Primary polycythaemia is also called polycythaemia vera. It happens right inside the bone marrow stem cells!

question: What is a primary goal of incorporating essential drugs into Nigeria's national health strategy?

options.A: To restrict healthcare services only to urban federal capitals
options.B: To ensure affordable access to life-saving treatments like malaria medications
options.C: To eliminate all traditional medicine practices across every region
options.D: To promote the sale of expensive imported brand-name syrups

explanation: Nigeria's policy uses the essential medicines framework to guarantee that common deadly conditions like malaria have available treatments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common system challenge in many healthcare settings?

options.A: Severe shortages of essential life-saving drugs
options.B: Excessive availability of well-trained nursing staff
options.C: Frequent interruptions in electrical power supply
options.D: Financial burdens caused by out-of-pocket payments

explanation: Spot on! Having too many well-trained staff is rare. Instead, staff shortages are a major challenge in resource-constrained systems.

question: Why do open-air transport methods pose a threat to public health?

options.A: They expose food to dust, exhaust fumes, and animal waste
options.B: They cause food items to freeze and lose their nutritional value
options.C: They prevent regulatory agents from collecting import duties
options.D: They force farmers to harvest crops before they are ripe

explanation: Uncovered or poorly protected transit exposes edible goods to environmental pollutants and biological contaminants. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h6)

question: Which substance serves as the main chemical building block for steroid hormones?

options.A: Tyrosine
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Nucleic acids
options.D: Cholesterol

explanation: Steroid hormones are made straight from cholesterol! Even though people often talk about cholesterol in a bad nutritional light, our bodies actually need it to build vital hormones.

question: What is often the primary cure for a hormone-secreting endocrine tumor?

options.A: Complete removal of the liver and spleen
options.B: Lifelong high-dose antibiotic therapy
options.C: Drinking large amounts of plain water
options.D: Surgical removal of the tumor

explanation: When an overactive gland or tumor is causing hypersecretion, cutting it out is usually the fastest and most direct cure. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h5)

question: In patient safety, what is a "near miss"?

options.A: A patient who successfully recovers from a major illness
options.B: An error that almost happened or was caught just before harming the patient
options.C: A medication that was prescribed but never manufactured
options.D: A nurse who arrived just seconds before her shift started

explanation: Wonderful! A near miss is a free warning sign that lets us fix problems before a real patient is hurt.

question: What is another name commonly used for leprosy?

options.A: Bright's disease
options.B: Lyme disease
options.C: Hansen's disease
options.D: Koch's disease

explanation: Leprosy is also called Hansen's disease, named after the scientist who discovered the causative bacterium. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h1)

question: What makes an interdisciplinary team different from a basic multidisciplinary team?

options.A: Interdisciplinary teams feature active communication and shared decision-making
options.B: Multidisciplinary teams always include community leaders and agriculture workers
options.C: Interdisciplinary teams restrict nurses from speaking during patient rounds
options.D: Multidisciplinary teams rely entirely on a single healthcare provider

explanation: Great thinking! While multidisciplinary teams work side-by-side, true interdisciplinary teams communicate closely and build care plans together.

question: What is a major safety worry when giving hypnotic medications to elderly patients?

options.A: Sudden permanent blindness upon waking
options.B: Falls resulting from daytime drowsiness and dizziness
options.C: Rapid development of severe bone fractures
options.D: Permanent loss of long-term childhood memories

explanation: Older adults can feel 'hangover' drowsiness the next day, which makes them super unsteady on their feet and prone to nasty falls.

question: For which patient condition is elective laparoscopy usually unsafe?

options.A: Stable asymptomatic gallstones
options.B: Mild controlled essential hypertension
options.C: A history of a single childhood hernia
options.D: Severe uncorrected bleeding disorders

explanation: Correct! If a patient has a severe bleeding problem that hasn't been fixed, putting in surgical instruments can cause dangerous internal bleeding.

question: Why is it risky to assume sudden confusion in an older adult is just 'normal aging'?

options.A: It automatically leads to permanent psychiatric institutionalization
options.B: It can cause nurses to miss acute illnesses like infections
options.C: It interferes with standard medication dosage calculations
options.D: It accelerates the natural hardening of the arteries

explanation: Great nursing insight! Never brush off sudden confusion as mere old age. It's often a red flag signaling a serious issue like a urinary tract infection or lack of oxygen.

question: What is the main benefit of placing a patient in the lateral (side-lying) position?

options.A: It maximizes lung expansion for asthma attacks
options.B: It takes weight off the sacrum and heels
options.C: It allows the patient to eat solid food safely
options.D: It provides direct access for urinary catheter insertion

explanation: Rolling a patient onto their side takes heavy pressure off the tailbone and heels, keeping their skin safe from bedsores!

question: What is the main job of corticosteroids when managing allergies and inflammation?

options.A: Instantly blocking H1 receptors on nerve endings
options.B: Reducing inflammation by suppressing the immune response
options.C: Dilating narrowed bronchial tubes within seconds
options.D: Neutralizing stomach acid to prevent digestive allergies

explanation: Spot on! Corticosteroids calm down an overactive immune system to bring down stubborn swelling and tissue irritation.

question: Which factor most directly worsens food spoilage during long-distance transport in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive use of modern pesticide sprays
options.B: High consumer demand for canned goods
options.C: Strict government border inspections
options.D: Lack of refrigerated transport vehicles

explanation: Without temperature control, fresh produce deteriorates rapidly in the tropical heat during transit. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h3)

question: What is the final practical step you should take before using a brand new checklist in a major study?

options.A: Translate the checklist into three new languages
options.B: Publish the checklist in a nursing journal
options.C: Pilot test the draft in a small trial run
options.D: File the checklist away in a locked cabinet

explanation: Always test-run your tool first! A pilot test helps catch confusing questions or missing steps before you start the real study.

question: An order calls for 500 mg of Paracetamol. The available tablets are 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?

options.A: 2 tablets
options.B: 1 tablet
options.C: 0.5 tablet
options.D: 4 tablets

explanation: Using the formula: (500 mg / 250 mg) × 1 tablet = 2 tablets. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the main nitrogen waste product created when the body breaks down protein?

options.A: Urea
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Protein metabolism naturally produces nitrogen waste, which the liver turns into urea for the kidneys to excrete. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h2)

question: How does a person's body build active immunity?

options.A: Through passive transfer of maternal antibodies across the placenta
options.B: Through genetic traits inherited directly from parents at birth
options.C: Through receiving temporary antibodies directly from an animal serum injection
options.D: Through the host's own immune system producing antibodies after exposure to a pathogen or vaccine

explanation: Active immunity means your body does the heavy lifting! Your own immune cells fight the germ (or vaccine) and remember it for the future.

question: When hospital managers look at research findings, what information do they care about the most?

options.A: Complex statistical formulas and raw data tables
options.B: Personal stories about individual patient feelings
options.C: Step-by-step instructions for changing wound dressings
options.D: Details on cost, efficiency, and policy changes

explanation: Spot on! Because administrators manage the hospital, they always look at how new findings impact resources, costs, and hospital policies.

question: Who was one of the very first industrial visiting nurses in the US, starting with Procter & Gamble in 1895?

options.A: Ada Mayo Stewart
options.B: Clara Barton
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Alice Hamilton

explanation: Ada Mayo Stewart provided great nursing care to workers and their families, setting an inspiring example for workplace health nurses.

question: Which factor is primarily responsible for urge faecal incontinence?

options.A: Excessive production of stomach acid
options.B: Weakened sphincters unable to hold back a strong bowel urge
options.C: Permanent blockage of the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Complete absence of the large intestine

explanation: In urge incontinence, the patient perceives the need to defecate, but weak muscles cannot keep the stool contained long enough to reach a toilet. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do clinical audits and incident reports help nursing management?

options.A: By ensuring that nurses never experience stress during their shifts
options.B: By replacing the need for formal hospital administrative authority
options.C: By automatically transferring legal liability to the hospital board
options.D: By providing control mechanisms to monitor performance and correct standard deviations

explanation: Audits and incident reports act as safety nets. They help managers spot mistakes early, track quality, and keep patient care standards high.

question: What is the big danger of planning a quality improvement project without asking bedside staff?

options.A: The proposed changes might be totally unworkable in busy clinical practice
options.B: Printing educational brochures will break the budget
options.C: Patients will stop taking their drugs completely
options.D: The hospital will instantly lose its official license

explanation: So true! Management might draw up rules that look amazing on paper, but if they don't fit the chaotic reality of a busy shift, they won't work. Always consult the bedside!

question: How does individualizing a medication schedule help a patient?

options.A: It allows the nurse to finish the shift much earlier
options.B: It lowers the financial cost of buying the medications from the pharmacy
options.C: It fits the drug timing into their normal daily routine to prevent missed doses
options.D: It stops the drug from causing any side effects in the body

explanation: When drugs match a person's daily habits, they are much easier to remember and take consistently. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which two tubes or openings empty directly into the vestibule area?

options.A: The urethra and the vagina
options.B: The fallopian tubes and ovaries
options.C: The ureters and the bladder
options.D: The uterus and the cervix

explanation: Spot on! The vestibule is the space containing the openings for both the urethra (urine) and the vagina.

question: What was the early nature of psychiatric facilities like the Yaba Lunatic Asylum when first opened?

options.A: Private luxury retreats for wealthy politicians
options.B: Holistic herbal healing camps run by local traditional leaders
options.C: Advanced community wellness centers with modern psychotherapy
options.D: Custodial holding centers modeled after harsh colonial asylums

explanation: Early colonial facilities in Nigeria were primarily designed for confinement and public safety rather than therapeutic rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) able to easily detect toxins in the blood?

options.A: It lacks any protective glial cells
options.B: It receives direct blood flow from the carotid artery
options.C: It contains a high concentration of pain receptors
options.D: It lies outside the blood-brain barrier

explanation: Spot on! Because the CTZ sits outside the strict blood-brain barrier, it can quickly spot chemicals or drugs floating in your bloodstream and warn the brain. Brilliant thinking!

question: What is the biggest perk of using a mixed methods design in nursing research?

options.A: It shortens the data collection phase to a single day
options.B: It provides a more complete picture by balancing numbers with human experience
options.C: It eliminates the need for any statistical calculations
options.D: It guarantees approval from all hospital ethical boards

explanation: Numbers tell us the 'how much,' but stories tell us the 'why.' Combining both gives us a much richer, more human understanding of healthcare challenges.

question: How can nurses best help prevent FGM within local communities?

options.A: By educating families and working with local leaders to change attitudes
options.B: By reporting every pregnant woman to international human rights courts
options.C: By offering safe, clean clinical alternatives for young girls
options.D: By focusing only on treating women who already have complications

explanation: Prevention relies on grassroots education and community engagement to address the root cultural drivers of FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the biggest risk of failing to track post-meeting action items?

options.A: Staff members will forget how to write clinical reports
options.B: The hospital will immediately fail its financial audit
options.C: Future meetings will become legally invalid
options.D: Decisions are forgotten and important tasks are left undone

explanation: Without tracking and follow-up, even the best plans discussed in meetings fade away into nothing.

question: What is the big pharmacokinetic perk of using sublingual and buccal routes?

options.A: Slower release over a 24-hour period
options.B: Avoidance of first-pass liver metabolism
options.C: Direct absorption into the lymphatic system
options.D: Destruction of the drug in the stomach

explanation: By soaking directly into the blood vessels in the mouth, the drug skips the trip through the liver, meaning more active medicine reaches the rest of the body intact!

question: What happens when political pressure forces hospital managers to price drugs below what it costs to replace them?

options.A: Fund insolvency and complete stock depletion
options.B: Immediate intervention by international drug manufacturers
options.C: Rapid expansion of hospital infrastructure
options.D: Excessive profits for the pharmacy department

explanation: When prices drop too low due to pressure, you simply won't have enough money to buy new stock when the current batch runs out. That leads straight to empty pharmacy shelves!

question: Why do doctors still order lab tests even when a male patient's physical symptoms look obvious?

options.A: Hospitals require blood tests for insurance billing purposes
options.B: Different STIs can present with very similar clinical signs
options.C: Antibiotics will not work without a written laboratory report
options.D: Physical exams cannot detect any form of genital infection

explanation: Many STIs look identical on the outside (like causing the same discharge or sores). Lab tests tell us the exact germ so we use the right drug.

question: Why is it important to note unexpected problems during the Do phase?

options.A: To make the paperwork as complicated as possible for staff
options.B: To prove to management that no changes were actually made
options.C: To ensure that nurses can be disciplined for making mistakes
options.D: To capture real-world challenges that will affect the study phase

explanation: Right! Knowing what went wrong in the busy clinical setting helps us understand our results much better later on.

question: What is the typical length range of a normal adult fallopian tube?

options.A: 5 to 7 centimeters
options.B: 2 to 4 centimeters
options.C: 10 to 12 centimeters
options.D: 20 to 25 centimeters

explanation: Standard adult fallopian tubes typically measure between 10 and 12 centimeters in length, though individual variations do occur. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h1)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a patient reacts badly to an IV medication?

options.A: Give an oral allergy tablet
options.B: Write down the exact time in the chart
options.C: Leave the room to find the doctor
options.D: Stop the medication infusion right away

explanation: Safety first! Stopping the drug immediately keeps any more of the bad stuff from entering the patient's body.

question: Which of these is a common reason why conflicts start in a hospital ward?

options.A: Ambiguous roles and unclear scopes of practice
options.B: Too many open nursing positions on the ward
options.C: An excess of available medical equipment
options.D: Identical personalities among all staff members

explanation: When people aren't quite sure where their duties end and someone else's begin, misunderstandings and friction are bound to happen.

question: Which of these is a common cultural barrier to good nutrition for some Nigerian teenage girls?

options.A: A total lack of local markets selling staple foods
options.B: Cultural food taboos that save protein-rich foods for adult males
options.C: Mandatory government laws banning green vegetables
options.D: Traditional ceremonies forcing teens to fast for whole months

explanation: True! Some traditional practices mistakenly keep young girls from eating nourishing foods like eggs, meat, or fish.

question: A nurse needs to assess circulation in a patient's foot after orthopedic surgery. Which pulse site should the nurse check?

options.A: Apical site
options.B: Brachial artery
options.C: Temporal artery
options.D: Dorsalis pedis

explanation: The dorsalis pedis pulse is located on the top of the foot and is used specifically to check blood flow to the lower extremities. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why do nurses encourage residents to do parts of their daily care on their own?

options.A: To test whether the resident is trying to escape from the facility
options.B: To comply with legal mandates that forbid nurses from assisting with bathing
options.C: To preserve resident dignity, maintain functional ability, and promote autonomy
options.D: To reduce the number of staff members needed on duty during night shifts

explanation: Brilliant! Encouraging self-care helps older adults stay active, independent, and proud of what they can still do.

question: A typhoid patient suddenly complains of severe, sharp belly pain and their tummy feels hard to the touch. What emergency does this point to?

options.A: Intestinal perforation
options.B: Renal stone formation
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Splenic rupture

explanation: Correct! A rigid tummy and sudden sharp pain are red flags for a perforated bowel—this needs urgent surgical help right away.

question: What is the primary enemy of dry food items stored in a pantry?

options.A: Darkness
options.B: Stagnant wind
options.C: Moisture
options.D: Cold air

explanation: Excess moisture causes dry goods like grains and flour to grow mold and attract pests. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h3)

question: What does a very large volume of distribution tell us about a drug?

options.A: The kidneys are getting rid of the drug too fast
options.B: The patient's liver is breaking down the medicine rapidly
options.C: The drug has moved heavily out of the blood and into body tissues
options.D: The drug is trapped strictly inside the blood vessels

explanation: A high volume of distribution means the drug loves hiding out in fat or muscle and leaves very little of itself floating behind in the blood.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three areas checked in the Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Eye opening response
options.B: Sensory touch response
options.C: Motor response
options.D: Verbal response

explanation: Remember the three main parts of GCS: Eyes, Verbal, and Motor! Sensory touch isn't part of it. A handy trick for exams and the ward.

question: Why must you check if two drugs are compatible before adding an IV piggyback medicine into an existing line?

options.A: Hospital pharmacy software blocks incompatible infusions anyway.
options.B: Primary fluids neutralize the therapeutic effect of all antibiotics.
options.C: Incompatible drugs can form precipitates that block the catheter.
options.D: Mismatched drugs will automatically cause severe patient hypertension.

explanation: Spot on! Mixing the wrong drugs can cause chemical reactions that turn into solid gunk, clogging the line and endangering the patient.

question: What is a major personal benefit of joining a professional nursing body as a student or young nurse?

options.A: Automatic pay raises negotiated by the national body
options.B: Guaranteed promotion to head nurse within a year
options.C: Opportunities for networking and career growth
options.D: Exemption from paying annual state license renewal fees

explanation: Joining lets you connect with senior nurses and mentors who can help guide your career path and open doors to exciting opportunities!

question: What must happen first to let blood drain out of the penis when an erection ends?

options.A: Rapid contraction of the somatic pudendal muscles
options.B: Sympathetic vasoconstriction of the helical arteries
options.C: Complete structural failure of the tunica albuginea
options.D: Parasympathetic release of large amounts of nitric oxide

explanation: You nailed the final one! Once the sympathetic nerves clamp down on the arteries, new blood stops rushing in, taking the pressure off the drainage veins so blood can finally flow out.

question: A patient has damage specifically in the vestibulocerebellum. What sign would you most expect to see?

options.A: Resting tremor in the upper extremities
options.B: Loss of conscious touch and vibration sensation
options.C: Truncal ataxia and balance impairment
options.D: Inability to plan multi-step writing tasks

explanation: Since the vestibulocerebellum looks after balance and steady posture, damage here makes it hard to stay upright, leading to a stumbling, wide stance. You are building fantastic clinical intuition!

question: If you're running a CBI and the drainage suddenly turns bright red with clots, what should you do with the drip rate?

options.A: Slow down the fluid flow to let the bladder rest
options.B: Stop the irrigation completely and clamp the catheter
options.C: Increase the drip rate until the output turns lighter
options.D: Disconnect the drainage bag to drain the clots faster

explanation: Speed things up! Running the fluid faster helps wash out the fresh blood and clots before they block the tube completely.

question: Which vitamin and mineral combination is most crucial for keeping older adults' bones strong?

options.A: Iron and vitamin C
options.B: Sodium and vitamin A
options.C: Potassium and magnesium
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: You got it! Calcium builds the bone, but vitamin D acts like the key that unlocks the door so the body can actually absorb that calcium.

question: What is the main way traditional family planning methods work?

options.A: They rely on behavioral practices and timing
options.B: They use barrier devices like condoms
options.C: They require daily hormonal pill ingestion
options.D: They involve minor surgical procedures

explanation: Traditional methods don't use drugs or devices. Instead, they depend on watching the menstrual cycle and modifying behavior around fertile days. You've got this!

question: What happens inside the small intestine of someone with celiac disease when they eat gluten?

options.A: Bacterial flora multiplies rapidly
options.B: Gastric acid production stops entirely
options.C: Excess mucus blocks digestion
options.D: Villi are damaged and flatten out

explanation: When gluten triggers an immune reaction in celiac disease, the tiny finger-like villi that absorb nutrients get flattened out. Great nursing insight to remember!

question: You notice a care assistant rushing an elderly resident through a meal. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Educate the assistant on patient-centered feeding techniques and safety
options.B: Report the assistant to the police for physical abuse immediately
options.C: Ignore the incident since assistants are trained separately
options.D: Take over feeding all residents in the facility personally

explanation: Well done! As a nurse, you supervise support staff. Teaching them the right, gentle way to feed residents ensures safe and dignified care.

question: Why do doctors check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and prolactin when investigating missed periods?

options.A: They measure the exact amount of blood stored in the uterine lining
options.B: Thyroid and pituitary disorders commonly disrupt normal reproductive hormones
options.C: They confirm whether the patient has an anatomical outflow blockage
options.D: They show if the ovaries have completely run out of egg follicles

explanation: Issues with your thyroid or high prolactin can easily mess up the delicate hormone signals needed for a regular period.

question: Your patient cries out in sharp pain as you inflate the catheter balloon. What is your very first move?

options.A: Stop inflation immediately and check if the catheter is still in the urethra
options.B: Push the catheter in harder to reach the proper depth
options.C: Inject the remaining water quickly to finish the procedure
options.D: Administer an oral painkiller and continue inflating

explanation: Stop right away! Pain during balloon inflation usually means the balloon is stuck inside the narrow urethra instead of resting safely in the bladder.

question: Which of these is NOT a standard step in AMTSL?

options.A: Controlled traction on the umbilical cord
options.B: Administration of a uterotonic drug
options.C: Routine manual removal of the placenta
options.D: Massage of the uterine fundus after delivery

explanation: Great job! We never pull the placenta out by hand routinely—that's only done if it fails to come out naturally with gentle cord traction.

question: Why does losing a massive amount of blood lead straight into shock?

options.A: The kidneys stop producing urine to save salt and water
options.B: Red blood cells multiply too fast and block small blood vessels
options.C: The heart beats too slowly to pump blood to the lungs
options.D: There is not enough fluid volume to maintain perfusion pressure

explanation: Without enough fluid in the pipes, the blood pressure drops, and vital organs don't get the blood flow they need. You're mastering the core concepts!

question: Why do community nurses rely heavily on basic anthropometric tools like measuring tapes?

options.A: Advanced hospital equipment is always brought to the field
options.B: Blood tests are illegal outside of licensed hospitals
options.C: Patients prefer tape measurements over physical examinations
options.D: They allow quick screening of large populations in remote areas

explanation: Remote clinics lack heavy laboratory equipment, so nurses use simple tools to screen many people efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: Who on the healthcare team is the go-to expert for designing specialized medical nutrition therapy?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The staff ward nurse
options.C: The registered dietitian
options.D: The attending physician

explanation: Dietitians have specialized training to create specific medical nutrition plans for patients with complex health needs.

question: Which resting position is best for improving circulation and comfort during pregnancy?

options.A: Sitting upright all night
options.B: Stomach prone position
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: Left lateral position

explanation: Lying on the left side takes the heavy uterus off major blood vessels, boosting blood flow to the baby and helping mum feel much more comfortable.

question: In an adult, where are new blood cells mostly made?

options.A: The outer layer of the spleen
options.B: The cortex of the kidneys
options.C: Yellow bone marrow
options.D: Red bone marrow

explanation: You nailed it! Red bone marrow found in flat bones and the ends of long bones is the busy factory floor where all new blood cells are born.

question: Why do nurses watch out specifically for waterborne diseases after heavy floods?

options.A: Excessive rainfall permanently destroys all local mosquito breeding grounds
options.B: Overflowing sewage systems mix with and contaminate drinking water sources
options.C: Damp weather conditions cause rapid airborne transmission of influenza
options.D: Standing water causes an immediate drop in local atmospheric oxygen levels

explanation: Floodwaters easily ruin sanitation systems, letting sewage leak into drinking water and spreading dangerous germs. Great to keep in mind for community health!

question: How does a community diagnosis help in measuring the success of a health program?

options.A: It guarantees that all diseases will be completely eradicated
options.B: It establishes baseline data before the program starts
options.C: It stops the community from asking for external financial help
options.D: It automatically cures chronic illnesses within the first month

explanation: You cannot measure progress or improvement later if you do not know what the health situation looked like in the beginning. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)
